clue.text: Thirty-two pieces in this musical composed

blocks.note: Chess is the 1980s stage musical by Tim Rice and the men of ABBA
to set words to music is to compose for them; set and composed both mean put together

explanation.surface: A musical with a cast of thirty-two numbers or players, all written specially for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' suggests pieces of music in a musical, but it means the board-game men; the definition is a description of what the answer contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard boxed chess game holds sixteen white and sixteen black men, making thirty-two playing items altogether.

clue.text: Border soldiers in the damaged landing zone

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the word next to it are rearranged
'in' puts the border and the soldiers inside the other, reworked word

blocks.note: a lip is the rim or edge of something
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
taken as written, then rearranged to wrap round the rest

explanation.surface: Frontier troops are stationed in a wrecked area where aircraft come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters of 'the' are scrambled and the border-plus-soldiers sits between their second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is an airfield built for helicopters, the place where such aircraft touch down and take off.

clue.text: Determined to have fire in south attended to

indicators.note: 'in' places the fire within the letters formed by south and attended to

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation
an ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook
to mind something is to look after it

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to keep a fire burning in the southern part of the house and look after it.
explanation.walkthrough: An ingle is an old word for a fire on the hearth, surviving in inglenook, the cosy corner beside a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone single-minded pursues a single aim with total resolve, which is what being determined means.

clue.text: Really old individual breaking leg

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: a leg of a journey or race is a stage of it
a single individual is one

explanation.surface: An extremely elderly person has broken their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works here as an adjective, as in 'stone-age equipment', so it swaps cleanly for 'Really old'.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period before metalworking is used informally as an adjective for anything hopelessly ancient or primitive.

clue.text: Asian to take place giant guards

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so the giant word goes around the other

blocks.note: the Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth
to be is to exist or occur, to take place

explanation.surface: A traveller from Asia is told to visit where a huge figure stands watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tibet, the Himalayan region on the Asian continent, is an inhabitant of Asia.

clue.text: What singers do that’s amazing in school?

indicators.note: 'in' puts the exclamation inside the abbreviation for school

blocks.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
'Cor!' is a British exclamation of amazement

explanation.surface: A question about what a school choir does that is so impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers' looks like vocalists, but here it means things that singe. Cor! is a British cry of surprise, like 'wow'.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn lightly, so things that singe are things that scorch, burning a surface.

clue.text: Old footballer training with the French

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is exercise training at school
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A retired footballer working out with a French team.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian forward who won three World Cups is among the most famous players of soccer's past.

clue.text: Path round university hospital in lakeside location

indicators.note: going round something means enclosing it, so the path surrounds what follows
here 'in' only joins the wordplay to the definition, which follows it

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow road or track
U is the abbreviation for university
a san, short for sanatorium, is a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: A track goes around a college medical centre in a town by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: San, short for sanatorium, is the old British boarding-school word for the sick bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss city stands on the northern shore of Lake Geneva, so it is a town beside a lake.

clue.text: American manoeuvres kept secret

indicators.note: manoeuvres are moves and repositionings, so the letters are shifted into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: US military exercises were held under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means held in private chambers, so proceedings conducted this way are hidden from the public.

clue.text: Details about loch needed for depressed Scots region

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information or details
L is a map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: Information about a Scottish lake is required for a gloomy part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' suggests unhappy, but it means low-lying, sunk below the land around.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley in Scotland, a stretch of land lying lower than its surroundings.

clue.text: Sandy, Broadway composer, leaving diamonds for dancer

indicators.note: when diamonds are leaving, that suit's letter departs from the composer's name

blocks.note: sandy and ginger both describe reddish hair
Richard Rodgers wrote Oklahoma! and The Sound of Music

explanation.walkthrough: Removing D from RODGERS leaves ROGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The American film star partnered Fred Astaire in a string of famous 1930s musicals and was celebrated for her dancing.

clue.text: Happy to do what Jason wanted?

blocks.note: golden describes a happy, flourishing time, as in golden days
to do someone is to swindle them, to fleece them

explanation.walkthrough: Jason and the Argonauts sailed in search of the ram's coat of gold in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero's quest aboard the Argo was to bring back the precious ram's hide from Colchis.

clue.text: Person, mellow, back in wine shop

blocks.note: bod is British slang for a person, short for body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mellow' is a verb here, not an adjective describing the person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish-speaking countries a bodega is a cellar or shop selling wine, and the word is borrowed for such stores.

clue.text: Parrot biting hard — cat finds point in orbit

indicators.note: biting something holds it between the jaws, so the parrot word grips the letter inside

blocks.note: to parrot or ape is to copy someone
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A parrot nips a hard-hearted cat, which then spots something in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a verb here, meaning to copy, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers use this term for the spot on a planet's or comet's path where it is farthest from the Sun.

clue.text: Disgraced religious figure rehashed new idea

indicators.note: to rehash is to rework old material into a new form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shamed holy man recycles an idea and passes it off as fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputation that is stained has been tarnished by scandal, which is what being disgraced involves.

clue.text: One holding shortened baton in biannual event

indicators.note: something shortened has been cut down, so the final letter is dropped
holding something means keeping it inside, so the one word encloses the other

blocks.note: sole means one and only
a baton is a stick, as a conductor's or relay runner's

explanation.surface: A lone runner holds a cut-down relay baton at an event held twice a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun reaches its northernmost and southernmost points twice each year, in June and December, giving the longest and shortest days.

clue.text: Make false accusations in case, losing case essentially

indicators.note: losing its case means the word gives up its outer covering, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the inner letters of the word left once its outside is stripped

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'case' is the word that loses its own case, leaving its middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to spread damaging, untrue claims about them, a formal verb for slander or defamation.

clue.text: Initial letters clue?

blocks.note: to initial a document is to sign it with your initials
letters arrive in the post, or mail

clue.text: Observe flood surrounding City close to Monument

the final letter of the landmark's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Monument is a column in the City of London commemorating the Great Fire of 1666; the City is the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to watch an event as an onlooker, so it is a verb for looking on, observing.

clue.text: Zero desire to protect the old with limited vision

blocks.note: the figure nought looks like the letter O
a need is a want or desire
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' is not elderly people but an old form of the word the.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sight in only a single eye restricts depth perception, and the word also means narrow or blinkered in outlook.

clue.text: Having litres to drink, help brought in as specified

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for litres

clue.text: Wayward son is a legendary Gaelic poet

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written

clue.text: Expert returned fruit to each diner for starters

the first letters of these three words

clue.text: Central Line for Cockney has eleven stops

clue.text: Hairy type having news-value occasionally

clue.text: Duke with debts hiding note wasn’t confident
